claim-auckland-001.text: The University of Auckland's Assessment of Courses Procedures state that AI use in assessment tasks may only be restricted when the task is a controlled assessment, identified as Lane 1; AI may be used without restriction in other assessment tasks, identified as Lane 2.

evidence.quote: In accordance with the University's two-lane approach, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in assessment tasks may only be restricted if the assessment task is a controlled assessment (lane 1). AI may be used without restriction in all other assessment tasks (lane 2).
evidence.location: Assessment design, item 7

claim-auckland-002.text: The University of Auckland's Assessment of Courses Procedures require courses to use the two-lane nomenclature, including telling students which assessments align with Lane 1 or Lane 2, and require courses and programmes to implement the two-lane approach in assessment design by 2027.

evidence.quote: Courses must use nomenclature of the two-lane approach, including specifying to students which assessments align with lane 1 or lane 2. Courses and programmes will be required to implement the two-lane approach in assessment design by 2027.
evidence.location: Assessment design, item 7

cl-university-of-auckland-gemini-301.text: Google Gemini is listed for University of Auckland in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.

evidence.quote: The University of Auckland provides all students and staff secure Google Gemini access approved by its Cybersecurity team. Secure access requires the University Google Workspace account ending @aucklanduni.ac.nz.

cl-university-of-auckland-microsoft-copi.text: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is listed for University of Auckland in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.

evidence.quote: The University of Auckland provides all students and staff secure Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat access approved by its Cybersecurity team. Users sign in with their University account through Edge or m365.cloud.microsoft/chat.

cl-university-of-auckland-notebooklm-303.text: Google Notebook LM is listed for University of Auckland in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.

evidence.quote: The University of Auckland provides all students and staff secure Notebook LM access approved by its Cybersecurity team. Secure access requires the University Google Workspace account ending @aucklanduni.ac.nz.

claim-auckland-003.text: The University of Auckland's student AI advice states that AI has no agency, treats the student prompting an AI tool as the author, and says students are ultimately responsible for work submitted for assessment.

evidence.quote: The university takes the position that AI has no agency. What this means is that the student who is prompting the AI tool is to be treated as the author. As the author, each student is responsible for the work generated by the AI tool, and this may include expressly acknowledging the use of the tool.
evidence.location: Artificial Intelligence in assessment

claim-auckland-004.text: The University of Auckland's permitted-software assessment guideline says Gen-AI may not be permitted for assessment activities where the assessed skills overlap with functions performed by Gen-AI, and says use of non-permitted software may be considered a breach of academic integrity.

evidence.quote: Generative AI (Gen-AI) may not be permitted for assessment activities where the skills assessed overlap with functions performed by Gen-AI. Use of software which is not permitted may be considered a breach of academic integrity and of the Student Academic Conduct Statute.
evidence.location: Guidelines: examples of tools and consequences of non-permitted software

claim-auckland-005.text: The University of Auckland TeachWell two-lane assessment guidance says the University does not endorse third-party AI detection tools, citing unreliability, false positives, and possible student-data training risks.

evidence.quote: The University of Auckland does not endorse the use of third-party AI detection tools, as these may be unreliable, create false positives, and may use student data to train their models.
evidence.location: FAQs: What about students who cheat? Can AI detection software help?

claim-auckland-007.text: Auckland Law School's student AI guidelines for taught courses state that using AI to generate, draft, or assist in creating content for graded assignments is prohibited unless the instructor explicitly permits it in writing.

evidence.quote: The use of AI to generate, draft, or assist in creating content for any graded assignment is prohibited, unless your instructor explicitly permits otherwise in writing (in your course outline or on Canvas).
evidence.location: The key principle

claim-auckland-006.text: The University of Auckland's public TeachWell explainer for the AI Usage Standard says users should assess data against the University's data classification before submitting it to an AI tool, and says restricted data should not be used with AI chat services.

evidence.quote: For example, it requires you to assess any data according to the University's data classification before you submit the data to an AI tool. The University has four data classifications: public, internal, sensitive, restricted. You should only use AI tools that are appropriate for the type of data you're working with.
evidence.location: Assess data sensitivity before using it with AI

claim-university-of-auckland-020.text: The University of Auckland says AI use may only be restricted in controlled Lane 1 assessment tasks.

evidence.quote: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in assessment tasks may only be restricted if the assessment task is a controlled assessment (Lane 1).
evidence.location: Two-Lane Approach section

claim-university-of-auckland-021.text: The University of Auckland says AI may be used without restriction in Lane 2 assessment tasks.

evidence.quote: AI may be used without restriction in all other assessment tasks (Lane 2).
evidence.location: Two-Lane Approach section

claim-university-of-auckland-022.text: The University of Auckland says all courses and programmes must implement the Two-Lane Approach in assessment design by 2027 unless a faculty specifies otherwise.

evidence.quote: All courses and programmes must implement the Two-Lane Approach in assessment design by 2027 unless differently specified by your faculty.
evidence.location: implementation timeline

claim-university-of-auckland-023.text: Auckland Law School says the graded-assignment AI prohibition applies to tools including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Microsoft Copilot, xAI, and similar tools.

evidence.quote: This prohibition applies to all generative AI systems, including but not limited to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Microsoft Copilot, xAI and similar tools.
evidence.location: key principle section

claim-university-of-auckland-024.text: Auckland Law School says permitted AI use for a specific assignment must be fully and accurately disclosed.

evidence.quote: If your instructor permits AI use for a specific assignment, you must disclose all AI use fully and accurately.
evidence.location: disclosure requirements section

claim-university-of-auckland-025.text: Auckland Law School tells students not to enter confidential, client, personal, proprietary, copyrighted, or legally protected information into AI tools.

evidence.quote: Do not enter: Confidential information... Client information... Personal information... Proprietary information... Copyrighted course materials... Information protected by privacy laws or professional duties.
evidence.location: privacy and confidentiality section

claim-university-of-auckland-026.text: Auckland Law School lists university-provided secure AI tools as Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, and NotebookLM when signed in with university accounts.

evidence.quote: The University provides access to generative AI tools with enhanced privacy protection when you sign in with your University account: Microsoft Copilot... Google Gemini... NotebookLM.
evidence.location: secure AI tools section

claim-university-of-auckland-027.text: The University of Auckland uses a Two-Lane Approach that distinguishes controlled assessments where AI use is restricted from other assessments where AI may be used.

evidence.quote: The two-lane approach differentiates between controlled assessments where AI use is restricted, and other assessments where AI may be used.
evidence.location: Two-Lane Approach section

claim-university-of-auckland-028.text: The University of Auckland says students are not permitted to use AI tools in Lane 1 assessments.

evidence.quote: Students are not permitted to use AI tools in Lane 1 assessments.
evidence.location: Lane 1 section

claim-university-of-auckland-029.text: The University of Auckland says students may use AI assistance without restriction in Lane 2 assessments.

evidence.quote: Students may use AI to assist them, and this use is not restricted.
evidence.location: Lane 2 section
